suggested_repairs.value: Hypothesis j also stops buying when every item of D_L(tau_j) carries a cached label: mu_D,L(tau_j) is then known exactly and replaces LCB_D(tau_j), H_j is rejected iff p_d^+ * (mu_D,L(tau_j) - slack) >= -epsilon, and otherwise the sequence stops.
suggested_repairs.delta_summary: T3 non-termination (|D_L(tau_j)| < B with a straddling interval loops forever). This adds the missing halting branch and leaves validity unchanged, because an exactly known mu_D,L needs no label-term width.

suggested_repairs.value: Set A(tau_0) to the empty set. For every j, before any label is bought for H_j, the bracket LCB_D - slack is floored at -1 (d >= -1), so H_j is rejected label-free whenever p_d^+(tau_j) <= epsilon. When p_d(tau_j) = 0 the shell selector and the Hoeffding slack are not evaluated.
suggested_repairs.delta_summary: T3 probes: the selector 0/0 and the slack's division by zero at p_d(tau_j)=0 for j<M, a label bought before a label-free certificate (main instance j=0,1), and an unfloored bracket (-0.00868 vs -0.00688).

suggested_repairs.value: with delta_lab + delta_pop = delta (split rule, fixed per hypothesis before any label is bought and computed from label-free quantities only: delta_pop is the smallest share for which the population slack, in Delta units, is at most the range-based label-term width at budget B; if no share in (0, delta) satisfies this, delta_pop is the share minimising the sum of the two widths)

This replaces the parenthetical '(split rule: assign delta_pop the smallest share that keeps its slack below the label-term width, since it is paid only in unlabeled counts)'.

suggested_repairs.value: The label advantage over a gold-only test at equal (epsilon, delta) holds when p_d is small. As p_d -> 1 the mechanism becomes a gold-only test run at delta_lab < delta plus a label-free slack floor of about sqrt(2 p_d ln(2/delta_pop)/|L|), so it then needs more gold labels than a gold-only anytime test at full delta.
suggested_repairs.delta_summary: T5/T4 regime: 'never worse ... at equal epsilon and delta' is refuted at p_d=1 (executed: 7923 vs 1109 labels, 3773 vs 691, 923 vs 259). This states the premise under which the claim can be kept.

suggested_repairs.value: The threshold grid is fixed before C and s_C are replayed on L_cert (or chosen on L_train), because the conditional-i.i.d. argument behind the Hoeffding slack on |D_L(tau_j)| and the fixed-sequence family-wise bound require A(tau_j) not to depend on L_cert.

regime.finding: The hook's guarantee 'never worse on their binding axis — gold labels per call site — at equal epsilon and delta' fails on the family p_d -> 1. When every call disagrees, the mechanism is a gold-only paired test that runs its labels at delta_lab < delta and also subtracts a label-free slack, so it needs more gold labels than a gold-only anytime test at full delta. The candidate's reasoning concedes that the method degrades to stratified gold-only testing, but it never says the result is worse than gold-only.
regime.why_not_repaired: The claim sits in `hook`, which this gate may edit only when a repair makes it factually wrong. The regime statement is suggested for core_mechanism_reasoning (W6), and the hook wording is left to the author and the audit.
regime.derivation: At p_d=1, D(tau)=A(tau), and the mechanism's lower bound is p_d^+ (LCB_{delta_lab} - slack). Here LCB at delta_lab < delta is at most the LCB at delta, slack > 0, and p_d^+ >= 1 multiplies a negative bracket. A gold-only test sampling L without replacement targets Delta_P directly at level delta with no slack. So at any fixed label count the mechanism's bound is at most the naive's, and labels-to-decision can only be larger.
regime.verbatim_step_quote: Against the strongest ground-truth certificates (a gold-only paired test; Conformal LLM Routing's Clopper-Pearson gate) it is never worse on their binding axis — gold labels per call site — at equal epsilon and delta
regime.executed_evidence: trace2.py, p_d=1 with B=|L|, eps=0.02, delta=0.05 (my values). |L|=20000, Delta_P=0.06: mechanism used 7923 labels (delta_pop=0.0334, delta_lab=0.01662, slack floor 0.0202) vs naive 1109. |L|=20000, Delta_P=0.08: 3773 vs 691. |L|=100000, Delta_P=0.06: 923 vs 259. The label-free floor sqrt(2 p_d ln(2/dp)/|L|) at p_d=1 is 0.0225 (|L|=20000, dp=0.0125) and 0.0071 (|L|=200000).

parameter_notes.finding: Step 5 has no halting rule once D_L(tau_j) is fully labelled before budget B is reached. With-replacement draws then hit the label cache forever (no label is bought, so the 'cumulative labels reach budget B' stop can never fire). Whenever the certified interval for Delta_P(tau_j) straddles -epsilon, neither the certify stop nor the futility stop fires and the loop does not terminate. Because the label-free slack does not shrink with labels, this straddle band has positive width for every finite |D_L|.
parameter_notes.why_not_repaired: This gate does not edit the candidate. A one-sentence definitional stop (W1) fixes it, and the assignment B <= |D_L(tau_1)| already guarantees halting, so it is a parameter-dependent defect rather than an impossibility.
parameter_notes.derivation: Labels are bought only for items of D_L(tau_j) not in the cache, and there are at most |D_L(tau_j)| of them. If cumulative labels plus |D_L(tau_j)| is less than B, the budget stop is unreachable. Once every item is cached, LCB_D converges to mu_D,L from below and UCB_D converges to mu_D,L from above. Certification needs p_d^+ (LCB_D - slack) >= -eps, and futility needs p_d^- (UCB_D + slack) < -eps (when negative). For any mu_D,L with p_d^+ (mu_D,L - slack) < -eps <= p_d^{+/-} (mu_D,L + slack), neither condition ever holds. Admissible assignment that halts: B <= |D_L(tau_1)|, since D_L(tau_j) is non-decreasing in j.
parameter_notes.verbatim_step_quote: stop when the certified bound on Delta_P(tau_j) clears -epsilon (move to j+1), when the confidence sequence's upper bound shows Delta_P(tau_j) < -epsilon, or when cumulative labels reach budget B (stop the sequence).
parameter_notes.executed_evidence: trace.py, probe 'D_L fully cached': |L|=2000, |D_L|=40 (20 items with d=-1, 6 with d=+1, 14 with d=0, so mu_D,L=-0.35), B=4000, delta=0.05, eps=0.02 (my values). Result: res='NO_HALT(guard 200000 draws, labels=40)', lcb_mu=-0.3639, slack_mu=0.4296, p_up=0.02972, lb_Delta=-0.02358. The same log with B=30 stops with res='budget'. Main instance, hypothesis j=4: the run labelled all 2144 items of D_L and then made 75,423 draws, certifying at lb_Delta exactly -0.02000, so it was one rounding step from the same stall.

parameter_notes.finding: The categorical shell selector Categorical(w_i/p_d(tau_j)) and the Hoeffding slack on |D_L(tau_j)| are undefined (0/0 and division by zero) for any hypothesis j with p_d(tau_j)=0. Step 3 states the label-free shortcut only for tau_M. Separately, the procedure never checks the label-free certificate before buying the first label, and it does not floor the bracket LCB_D - slack at -1.
parameter_notes.why_not_repaired: Definitional; W2 states the intended label-free rule for every j. A grid whose first migrated set A(tau_1) contains at least one disagreement avoids the division, so this is a parameter (grid) edge, not an impossibility.
parameter_notes.derivation: w_i/p_d(tau_j) with p_d(tau_j) = sum_{i<=j} w_i = 0 is 0/0. The slack sqrt(2 ln(2/delta_pop)/|D_L(tau_j)|) with |D_L(tau_j)|=0 divides by zero. Because d >= -1, Delta_P >= -p_d,P >= -p_d^+, so H_j is certifiable with zero labels whenever p_d^+ <= eps. The bracket (LCB_D - slack) can drop below -1, which only loosens the bound.
parameter_notes.verbatim_step_quote: if p_d(tau_M) = 0 the full-migration certificate is immediate up to the label-free slack.
parameter_notes.executed_evidence: trace.py, probe p_d=0: an all-agree log of 1000 records gives 'p_d=0: selector w_i/p_d is 0/0 and slack sqrt(.../|D_L|) divides by 0'. Python raises ZeroDivisionError on 0/0.0. Main instance, j=0: p_d,L=0.00535, p_up=0.00688, slack=0.2626. The unfloored bound p_up*(-1-slack) = -0.00868 and the floored bound p_up*(-1) = -0.00688 both clear -0.02, yet one label was bought before the check (labels_cum=1). The same happened at j=1.

parameter_notes.finding: The delta-split rule ('assign delta_pop the smallest share that keeps its slack below the label-term width') has no solution in (0, delta) whenever the unlabeled disagreement count |D_L(tau_j)| is not well above the label budget, and the text gives no fallback. The rule is also circular until 'label-term width' is pinned to a label-free quantity: under the reading 'observed CS width', the level delta_lab is chosen from the labels it then certifies.
parameter_notes.why_not_repaired: This is a wording/definition issue (W3). Admissible assignments exist where the rule is feasible (for example |L|=200000 with B=4000, or B=1000 with |L|=20000), so it is a parameter finding.
parameter_notes.derivation: Under reading (a), with the label-term width taken as range-based at budget B: pop width ~ p_d sqrt(2 ln(2/dp)/(p_d |L|)) and label width = p_d sqrt(2 ln(1/dl)/B). Their ratio is ~ sqrt(B ln(2/dp) / (|D_L| ln(1/dl))). Since ln(2/dp) > ln(1/dl) near the crossing, the ratio exceeds 1 for every dp in (0, delta) whenever |D_L| is at most about B, so the 'smallest share' does not exist. Under reading (b), with the label-term width taken as the observed confidence-sequence width, the split depends on the labels, and the level-delta guarantee then needs a separate argument.
parameter_notes.verbatim_step_quote: with delta_lab + delta_pop = delta (split rule: assign delta_pop the smallest share that keeps its slack below the label-term width, since it is paid only in unlabeled counts)
parameter_notes.executed_evidence: trace2.py feasibility scan over dp = delta*k/400 with delta=0.05: (p_d=0.107, |L|=20000, B=4000, nD=2140) gives feasible=False. (0.107, 20000, B=1000) gives feasible=True with first dp=0.04925. (0.107, |L|=200000, B=4000) gives feasible=True with first dp=0.01775. (0.01, 20000, 4000) gives feasible=False. (0.01, 1000000, 4000) gives feasible=True. In the main instance every j was infeasible (for example j=0: popw=0.00333 vs labw=0.00036), and my script fell back to dp=0.04988, leaving delta_lab=0.000125.
parameter_notes.reading_dependence: reading_dependent: infeasibility holds under reading (a) (range-based width at budget B, label-free); the circularity concern holds under reading (b) (observed CS width)
